# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_WIDTH_COMPRESSION_TO_EXPANSION_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Tight EMA ribbon compression followed by expansion breakout captures impending volatility bursts. Low ribbon width indicates low volatility equilibrium; expansion signals imminent volatility expansion. This exploits the mean-reversion to expansion cycle in EMA ribbon dynamics.

## Mechanism

Compute ribbon width = (highest EMA - lowest EMA) / ATR(14) using 9, 12, 26 EMAs. When width < 0.3 for three consecutive bars, enter long if close > highest EMA and volume > 1.2 * 20-bar average volume; enter short if close < lowest EMA and volume > 1.2 * 20-bar average volume. Exit: chart-stop at opposite ribbon extreme (long: stop below lowest EMA; short: stop above highest EMA), TP1 at 2R, runner trail 20% off HWM. Regime filter: only trade when VIX < 18; avoid when VIX > 28.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account ~= 14% headline P&L (based on $0.50–$2.00 entry premium zone and 50% per-trade risk cap).
2. **Sample bias:** No historical backtest performed; proposal based on theoretical volatility expansion concept. High overfit risk due to untested parameters (width threshold, consecutive bars, volume multiplier).
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward or held-out window tested).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic OPRA simulation on top 3 J days).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: whipsaw in choppy markets (multiple false breakouts); max drawdown: consecutive losses during failed breakouts; blow-up scenario: volatility expansion without follow-through (expansion traps) during low-liquidity periods.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (if top-5 days = X% of P&L, X cannot be estimated without backtest).
